description: Sixteen-voice sample player with a separate sample for each channel, and a filter on every channel

params.text: Sets where in that channel's sample it starts, the beginning at one end and the end at the other
Sets how much of that channel's sample is played from its start point, none at one end and all of it at the other
Loops that channel's slice while the gate is held, on the gate setting
Sets how fast that channel reads its sample, stopped at 0 and ten times at the top, and the pitch rises with it
Switches that channel between playing its slice right through on a trigger and playing only while the gate is held
Sets that channel's filter frequency, 22Hz at one end and 16384Hz at the other
Picks that channel's filter — off, low-pass, band-pass or high-pass
Chooses which of the sixteen channels the controls are editing, 0 to 15; every channel keeps its own sample and settings
Picks a channel this one stops as soon as that channel starts playing, or OFF for none, which is how a closed hi-hat is made to cut an open one

inputs.text: Starts a channel playing; it is polyphonic, and the channel that plays is the polyphony channel the trigger arrives on
0V to 10V switches that channel between playing right through on a trigger and playing only while the gate is held
0V to 10V moves that channel's start point across the whole sample, added to the knob
0V to 10V adds to that channel's length across its whole range
0V here turns that channel's loop off
0V to 10V adds to that channel's speed, up to ten times
0V to 10V adds to that channel's filter resonance across its whole range
0V to 10V adds to that channel's filter frequency across its whole range
0V to 10V picks that channel's filter, stepping through off, low-pass, band-pass and high-pass
0V to 10V picks which channel each channel stops, from OFF at 0V through the sixteen channels

outputs.text: The sixteen channels, one per polyphony channel; use a split module to take them apart

notes: nothing plays until a sample is loaded, and each channel holds its own: select the channel first, then choose Load sample from the right-click menu, or drop a wav or aiff file onto the panel
samples are played in mono, so a stereo file is mixed down as it is loaded, and a file recorded at another rate is converted to the engine's sample rate
menu: Load sample — opens a wav or aiff file and loads it into the channel that is selected
